coverage.notes: SEL: North Dakota has NDMTSS SEL Goals (June 2018, K-12, four grade spans, five CASEL-named competencies), led and funded by the DPI's MTSS project. Their own introduction says freestanding SEL standards do not currently exist in ND and points to a crosswalk of SEL embedded in content standards; DPI's SEL page calls the goals a framework to guide instruction, so I chose guidance_only. NOTE: DPI's live SEL page returned HTTP 403 to my downloads, so I read an Internet Archive copy (Sept 2022) of that page and Archive copies (Aug 2022 capture) of the four goal PDFs it links on ndrea.org; the live ndrea.org links are gone. I could not confirm the goals are unchanged since 2018. Portrait of a Graduate: DPI's Learning Continuum page (read live) states ND's Portrait of a Graduate was unveiled by Governor Burgum at the 2021 Summit on Innovative Education and lists seven attributes; I read the DPI PDF. Reviewer: confirm the live SEL page and any newer SEL document.

frameworks.name: North Dakota MTSS Social and Emotional Learning Goals
frameworks.issuingBody: North Dakota Department of Public Instruction (NDMTSS project)
frameworks.notes: Read in Internet Archive copies (capture 2022-08-12) of the documents DPI's SEL page links, originally at ndrea.org/assets/docs/NDMTSS SEL Goals/: '6-1-18 NDMTSS SEL Learning Goals Introduction.pdf', '...Goals by Competancy.pdf', '...Goals by Grade-level.pdf' and 'Compiled NDMTSS SEL Scales.pdf' (all dated June 2018). Not formal standards: the introduction says freestanding SEL standards do not exist in ND. Each of the five competencies has 4-6 numbered goals per grade span (K-2, 3-5, 6-8, 9-12); the goals are not tied one-to-one to named indicators, so items here are the five competencies only, with summaries I wrote from the goal themes. The goals are named after and organized by CASEL's five competencies, so caselCompetency is the document's own structure. Year 2018 is the document date, not an adoption date.

items.title: Recognizing emotions, strengths and limits, and asking for help
items.summary: Across K-12 goals: label emotions and what triggers them, link emotions to behavior, identify strengths and interests, build a growth mindset, recover from setbacks, seek help, and advocate for oneself.

items.title: Regulating emotions and pursuing goals
items.summary: Across K-12 goals: self-control, handling stress and emotions, taking responsibility, self-motivation, setting and monitoring goals, and planning, prioritizing and managing time.

items.title: Empathy, respect, and using supports
items.summary: Across K-12 goals: identify others' feelings and perspectives, appreciate individual and cultural differences, oppose stereotyping, ask for help, and use home, school and community resources.

items.title: Communication, teamwork, and conflict resolution
items.summary: Across K-12 goals: verbal, non-verbal and electronic etiquette, social participation, giving and receiving feedback, making friends, teamwork, limit setting, and resolving conflict.

items.title: Solving problems and weighing consequences
items.summary: Across K-12 goals: define and solve problems, weigh consequences, tell safe from risky behavior, use refusal skills, take responsibility, notice outside influences, and apply ethical standards.

frameworks.name: North Dakota's Portrait of a Graduate
frameworks.issuingBody: North Dakota Department of Public Instruction
frameworks.notes: Read in DPI's PDF https://www.nd.gov/dpi/sites/www/files/documents/Academic%20Support/ND%20Learning%20Continuum/FinalNoDakPOG.pdf (linked from the Learning Continuum page, which says it was unveiled in 2021 and supports alternate pathways to graduation). Seven attributes, each with 2-4 'A North Dakotan...' statements; summaries are my paraphrases. The PDF itself shows no date and one secondary source (KnowledgeWorks) says 2020, so the 2021 year comes from the DPI page only; reviewer should confirm. Not mapped to CASEL competencies by the state.

items.title: Critical Thinking
items.summary: Improves the quality of one's own thinking by questioning bias and assumptions, thinks clearly and open-mindedly, and weighs global and local effects of solutions.

items.title: Communication
items.summary: Listens to understand, expresses ideas effectively in varied forms, and communicates for different purposes, including self-advocacy, relationships, conflict resolution and feedback.

items.title: Empathy
items.summary: Seeks to understand and respond to others' views, feelings and experiences, takes responsibility for making the world better, and accepts that societal challenges need compromise.

items.title: Collaboration
items.summary: Takes shared responsibility, uses strengths to build collective commitment, contributes to group effectiveness, and draws out diverse perspectives.

items.title: Learner's Mindset
items.summary: Commits to lifelong learning with passion and is willing to learn, unlearn and relearn.

items.title: Adaptability
items.summary: Responds productively to feedback, setbacks and criticism, balances differing views to reach workable solutions, and plans using self-awareness and self-management.

items.title: Perseverance
items.summary: Understands how effort, attitude and achievement connect, treats failure as part of success, handles adversity using strengths and supports, and shows grit and curiosity.

alignments.framework: North Dakota MTSS Social and Emotional Learning Goals
alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Stay in Control of Your Spirit" (series: Conflict & Self-Government; the objective is the same in every grade version). FNE's stated objective: "Learners will identify signs that emotions are beginning to take control, practice a simple pause-and-reset process, and choose one respectful action that keeps their response aligned with their values." The lesson has students recognise when emotions start driving behaviour and choose a response, which is the same skill.

FNE's stated objective: "Students will understand that knowing their limits is not weakness.
